claim: Daude, Kamran and Nicoleau prove that the Steklov spectrum of a compact warped-product Riemannian manifold with connected boundary determines the warping function uniquely, and that approximate knowledge of the Steklov spectrum (in a precisely defined sense) already determines it uniquely near the boundary.
stance_target: does a quantitative stability theorem for an inverse spectral problem exist anywhere, on any manifold class, published in the target venue (JGA)
scope_conditions: compact manifolds with connected boundary equipped with a warped-product metric, generalized deformed balls in R^d
quoted_support: We first prove that the Steklov spectrum determines uniquely the warping function of the metric. We show in fact that the approximate knowledge (in a given precise sense) of the Steklov spectrum is enough to determine uniquely the warping function in a neighbourhood of the boundary.

claim: Daude-Kamran-Nicoleau provide stability estimates of log-type on the warping function recovered from the Steklov spectrum, using a formula connecting the inverse spectral data to the Laplace transform of the difference of the two warping factors.
stance_target: the standard modulus of continuity achieved in quantitative inverse spectral stability results, when achieved at all, is logarithmic (severe ill-posedness), matching the Alessandrini-type log-stability pattern from related inverse problems
quoted_support: Second, we provide stability estimates of log-type on the warping function from the Steklov spectrum. The key element of these stability results relies on a formula that, roughly speaking, connects the inverse data (the Steklov spectrum) to the Laplace transform of the difference of the two warping factors.

claim: The Journal of Geometric Analysis has published a quantitative-stability inverse spectral theorem (Daude-Kamran-Nicoleau, vol. 31, 1821-1854, DOI 10.1007/s12220-019-00326-9), establishing that the target venue for the planned theorem already accepts this genre of result, though the setting studied (smooth warped-product manifolds) is not an orbifold, cone, or corner setting.
stance_target: venue precedent for a stability theorem in inverse spectral geometry
quoted_support: Daude, T., Kamran, N. & Nicoleau, F. Stability in the Inverse Steklov Problem on Warped Product Riemannian Manifolds. J Geom Anal 31, 1821-1854 (2021).
